title: Nursing Note - ICU Arrival / Admission
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Admission to BICU-6 from ED with bedside handoff and full head-to-toe assessment; Parkland LR 450 mL/h, goal UOP 30-50 mL/h.
body:
**Handoff**
- Arrived BICU-6 at 04:00 from ED with A. Torres, RN. Bedside SBAR handoff and two-identifier check done (name/DOB, MRN SIM-40101). 34 y/o M, 82 kg, flame burn 22% TBSA + smoke inhalation from house fire ~01:30. NKDA. Full Code. Admit orders (04:10) verified against handoff.
- ED course: EMS LR 500 mL; L AC PIV 02:40; Foley 02:45; intubated 02:50; OG 03:05; R forearm/hand escharotomy 03:15; Tdap 03:30; L IJ CVC 03:45. COHb 14.2% (02:50) -> 6.4% (04:15); lactate 5.8 -> 3.4. Dr. Brandt performed bedside bronchoscopy 04:20: grade 2 inhalation injury (erythema, soot, mucosal edema), ETT left in place.

**Vitals (04:00)**
- HR 106 ST, BP 101/58 (MAP 72), RR 17, SpO2 100% (falsely reassuring with elevated COHb), T 97.4 °F bladder. POC glucose 148.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: sedated, RASS -3 (goal -2 to -3) on propofol 30 mcg/kg/min + fentanyl 100 mcg/h. Pupils 3 mm, equal, brisk. Does not follow commands; withdraws L arm to stimulus. CPOT 1/8.
- Resp: 8.0 oral ETT 24 cm at teeth, secured. AC/VC VT 450, set RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0; PIP 28/Pplat 21. BS coarse with scattered rhonchi bilaterally, no wheeze. Small black-flecked carbonaceous secretions on suction; perioral soot, singed nasal hairs.
- CV: ST, no ectopy. Generalized edema starting. L radial 2+, cap refill 2 s L hand. R hand: Doppler radial and ulnar signals present and strong after escharotomy (marked with skin marker); exposed nail beds warm.
- GI: OG 16 Fr to low intermittent suction, 30 mL green-clear; abdomen soft, nondistended, bowel sounds hypoactive x4. NPO.
- GU: Foley 16 Fr with temp probe, dark amber urine (SG 1.031 on ED UA, myoglobin negative); ED-reported UOP ~25 mL/h.
- Skin: R arm circumferential 9% - forearm/hand full-thickness (waxy, leathery, insensate), upper arm deep partial (mottled, weeping). Anterior chest 9% deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches. Face/neck 4% superficial to superficial partial (erythema, small blisters). Total 22% TBSA (~8% full-thickness). Escharotomy incisions dressed, minimal ooze. R arm on pillows above heart, hand splinted in position of function. Back/legs intact.
- Lines: L IJ triple-lumen CVC (tip at cavo-atrial junction per CXR), CHG dressing intact; L AC 18 g PIV patent, no infiltration. Arterial line to be placed by Dr. Brandt.

**Resuscitation**
- Parkland 4 x 82 x 22 = 7,216 mL/24 h from 01:30 (3,608 mL in first 8 h, EMS 500 mL counted). LR 450 mL/h via CVC. Hourly UOP goal 30-50 mL/h (41 mL/h = 0.5 mL/kg/h); notify burn team if <30 mL/h x2 h or <20 mL/h.

**Safety / family**
- Soft L wrist restraint (ETT/line protection), skin intact, restraint order requested; contact precautions; suction, BVM at bedside; HOB 30; low air loss mattress.
- Jenna Whitaker (partner) at bedside, updated and oriented to unit, visiting rules, gown/glove. Clothing not salvageable; wallet/phone and ring (removed in ED) given to Jenna. Daughter Ava is safe with family.

title: Nursing Note - Arterial Line and Hourly Neurovascular Check
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: L radial arterial line placed 04:30 by Dr. Brandt, waveform and zeroing verified; hourly R hand Doppler check unchanged; UOP 25 mL for 04-05.
body:
**Arterial line**
- L radial 20 g arterial line placed 04:30 by Dr. Brandt (R arm burned). Modified Allen test normal pre-procedure. Sterile technique with full barrier and CHG prep; secured with sutures, transparent dressing and arm board, site clean/dry, no hematoma.
- Transducer leveled and zeroed to air at the phlebostatic axis. Pressure bag 300 mmHg, flush running. Waveform crisp with dicrotic notch; fast-flush square wave test acceptable (not over- or underdamped). Art BP 99/55 (MAP 70) correlates with NIBP L arm within 5 mmHg. First ABG drawn from line without difficulty.
- L hand checked q2h for line complications: warm, pink, cap refill 2 s, normal motion/sensation not assessable (sedated), no blanching.

**Hourly R arm/hand neurovascular check (05:00)**
- Doppler: radial and ulnar signals present, strong biphasic, unchanged from 04:00. Digital signals present digits 2-5.
- Forearm soft and compressible above and below the escharotomy; incisions open with minimal serosanguineous ooze. Fingertips warm, no pallor, no cyanosis. Cap refill in exposed nail beds ~3 s (burn edema). No new tension. Arm elevated on pillows above heart; splint intact, not constricting.
- Burn team to be called immediately for loss of Doppler signal, pallor, tense forearm or escalating pain response.

**Other**
- Vitals 05:00: HR 109 ST, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 18, SpO2 99%, T 97.6 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. PIP 28/Pplat 21, FiO2 1.0.
- I&O 04:00-05:00: in 537 mL, UOP 25 mL (0.30 mL/kg/h), dark amber - below 30 mL/h goal for the first hour. LR continues 450 mL/h. Will re-evaluate at 06:00 and call the burn team if UOP remains below 30 mL/h for a second consecutive hour.
- 06:00 labs and ABG due; heparin SQ and acetaminophen IV also due 06:00.

title: Nursing Note - Resuscitation Fluid Titration
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: UOP 25 and 26 mL/h x2 hours; Dr. Okafor called, LR increased 450 to 540 mL/h at 06:00.
body:
**Trigger**
- UOP 04:00-05:00 = 25 mL (0.30 mL/kg/h) and 05:00-06:00 = 26 mL (0.32 mL/kg/h): below the 30 mL/h goal for two consecutive hours per Parkland titration protocol. Urine concentrated, dark amber.

**SBAR to Dr. Okafor (burn surgery), called 05:55**
- S: UOP below goal x2 h on LR 450 mL/h.
- B: 34 y/o M, 22% TBSA flame burn + inhalation injury, 82 kg, Parkland goal 3,608 mL in first 8 h (450 mL/h average from 02:30).
- A: HR 109 ST, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 17, SpO2 100%, T 97.8 °F; lactate 3.4 at 04:15 (down from 5.8). No signs of volume overload; ventilator PIP 28/Pplat 21, unchanged. Bladder pressure checked at 05:30 = 12 mmHg (goal <15). R hand Doppler radial/ulnar signals present, forearm soft, no pallor. Foley patent, no kinks, bladder not distended, flushed per protocol without clot. UA 02:55 myoglobin negative.
- R: increase LR by 20%.
- Order received and read back: LR 450 -> 540 mL/h. Rate changed on the pump with a second RN check at 06:00.

**Reassessment plan**
- Continue hourly UOP, goal 30-50 mL/h (41 mL/h = 0.5 mL/kg/h); recheck at 07:00 and again hourly. If UOP rises above 50 mL/h x2 h the rate will be decreased 20-25%. Notify for UOP <20 mL/h x1, MAP <65, rising PIP/Pplat, bladder pressure >15 mmHg, or any change in R hand signals.
- Soft L wrist restraint order now active (06:00); skin and circulation checked, intact.
- FiO2 weaned from 1.0 to 0.6 at 06:00 by RT (COHb 6.4% at 04:15, PaO2 288). 06:00 BMP/Mg/Phos drawn; heparin SQ 5,000 units and acetaminophen 1,000 mg IV given 06:00.

title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Summary / Handoff to Day RN
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Night summary and handoff to day RN: lines, drips, FiO2 0.6, COHb trend, upcoming care.
body:
**Summary 04:00-06:50**
- Admitted from ED 04:00 with grade 2 inhalation injury and 22% TBSA flame burn. Hemodynamically stable on LR alone; no pressors. Vitals 06:00: HR 109 ST, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 17, SpO2 100%, T 97.8 °F (rewarming with warm blankets and warmed room).
- Neuro: RASS -3, CPOT 1/8 on propofol 30 mcg/kg/min + fentanyl 100 mcg/h. Pupils equal, brisk.
- Resp: 8.0 ETT 24 cm at teeth. AC/VC VT 450, RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 weaned 1.0 -> 0.6 at 06:00. PIP 28/Pplat 21. Carbonaceous secretions decreasing. COHb 14.2% (02:50) -> 6.4% (04:15); next ABG/COHb 08:00. Keep SpO2 goal >=94% until COHb normal.

**Lines / drips**
- L IJ CVC: distal LR 540 mL/h, medial propofol, proximal fentanyl. L AC 18 g PIV saline-locked for IV meds. L radial A-line (placed 04:30): waveform good, bag 300 mmHg, zeroed this shift; L hand perfusion normal. OG to LIS; Foley to gravity bag with hourly UOP; contact precautions.

**Fluids**
- LR 450 -> 540 mL/h at 06:00 per Dr. Okafor for UOP 25 and 26 mL/h. UOP 06:00-07:00 pending (goal 30-50). Parkland 7,216 mL/24 h from 01:30; 3,608 mL by 09:30.

**R arm**
- Hourly Doppler checks: radial/ulnar signals present all hours, forearm soft, no pallor. Arm elevated, splint on. Bladder pressure 12 mmHg at 05:30.

**Family / safety**
- Jenna at bedside most of the night, updated, resting in family room. L wrist soft restraint on; skin intact.

**Coming up**
- 07:00 heparin neb; 08:00 ABG with COHb, albuterol neb; 09:00 pantoprazole, vitamins and chlorhexidine; 09:30 Parkland hour 8 - LR rate change expected per Dr. Okafor; trophic feeds anticipated 10:00; 12:00 labs incl. CK; 14:00 first dressing change with burn nurse. Dietitian, PT/OT and case management consults pending.

title: Nursing Note - Day Shift Assessment
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Day shift head-to-toe assessment after bedside handoff from E. Haddad, RN; stable on LR 540 mL/h.
body:
**Handoff / safety**
- Bedside handoff from E. Haddad, RN at 07:00 with lines, drips, alarms and restraint checked. ID band verified. Contact precautions. Bed low, HOB 30, suction and BVM at bedside.

**Vitals (07:00)**
- HR 111 ST, BP 99/57 (MAP 71), RR 18, SpO2 99%, T 98.2 °F bladder.

**Systems**
- Neuro: RASS -3 on propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. Pupils 3 mm equal brisk. CPOT 1/8. No spontaneous following of commands (appropriate for goal).
- Resp: 8.0 ETT 24 cm at teeth, secure, lip-side skin intact. AC/VC VT 450, RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.6; PIP 28/Pplat 21. BS coarse bilaterally, small amount of gray-tinged thin secretions on suctioning. Heparin neb given 07:00.
- CV: sinus tachycardia 111, no ectopy. MAP 71 (goal >=65). Generalized edema, face and chest swelling, expected. L hand warm, cap refill 2 s. R hand: radial and ulnar Doppler signals present, forearm soft, no pallor; arm elevated and splinted.
- GI: OG to low intermittent suction, small green-clear output; abdomen soft, nondistended, bowel sounds hypoactive. NPO pending feeding order.
- GU: Foley patent, urine dark amber turning amber. UOP 06:00-07:00 33 mL (0.40 mL/kg/h) on LR 540 mL/h - improving but still below the 41 mL/h target.
- Skin: R arm and chest dressings dry and intact, minimal serosanguineous strike-through at escharotomy sites. Face: erythema, blistering, no new drainage. Back and heels intact; low air loss mattress.
- Lines: L IJ CVC CHG dressing intact, no erythema; L AC 18 g patent; L radial A-line site clean, art BP matches NIBP.
- Restraint: soft L wrist, circulation, skin and sensation intact.

**Plan**
- Hourly UOP, titrate LR per Dr. Okafor; 08:00 ABG/COHb; turn q2h; Parkland phase change at 09:30; dressing change 14:00.

title: Nursing Note - Parkland Phase 2 / Morning Care
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: LR changed to 225 mL/h at 09:30 (hours 8-24 from injury); UOP trend; pantoprazole, oral care and vitamins given.
body:
**Fluid resuscitation**
- First 8 h of Parkland complete at 09:30 (01:30 injury time): 500 mL EMS + ED/ICU LR, about 3,965 mL given vs 3,608 mL goal. Per Dr. Okafor's order LR rate changed 540 -> 225 mL/h at 09:30 (second half of 7,216 mL goal over hours 8-24, to be titrated hourly to UOP). Rate verified with second RN.
- UOP trend: 06-07 33 mL, 07-08 40 mL, 08-09 44 mL (0.54 mL/kg/h); current hour pending. Urine light amber. Goal 30-50 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h = 41). Will notify burn team for UOP <30 mL/h x2 h or >50 mL/h x2 h.

**Vitals (09:00)**
- HR 108 ST, BP 103/60 (MAP 74), RR 17, SpO2 99%, T 98.5 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. PIP 28/Pplat 21 on FiO2 0.6, PEEP 5.

**Labs**
- 08:00 ABG: pH 7.38, PaCO2 40, PaO2 172, HCO3 23, COHb 3.1%, lactate 2.2 (improving). 06:00 BMP: K 4.5, Ca 8.4, Cr 0.9, glucose 156. Troponin 0.02 at 08:50 (second, unchanged).

**Medications / care (09:00)**
- Pantoprazole 40 mg IV (stress ulcer prophylaxis). Chlorhexidine 0.12% oral rinse 15 mL (VAP bundle). Via OG: vitamin C 500 mg, zinc 220 mg, multivitamin with minerals, thiamine 100 mg and folic acid 1 mg - OG clamped 30 min then returned to LIS. Bacitracin thin layer to face.
- Albuterol neb 08:00 and heparin neb 07:00 per inhalation protocol; acetylcysteine due 11:00.
- Turned and repositioned off R arm and chest, R arm re-elevated on pillows; skin on sacrum/heels intact.

**Neurovascular**
- Hourly R hand checks: Doppler radial/ulnar present, forearm soft, no pallor. L hand A-line site OK.

**Plan**
- Trophic tube feeds planned 10:00. Continue hourly UOP and neurovascular checks; family update by Dr. Okafor at rounds; Jenna at bedside.

title: Nursing Note - Enteral Feeding Initiation
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Osmolite 1.5 started at 20 mL/h via OG at 10:00; tolerance, HOB 30, glucose 164.
body:
**Feeding start**
- Tube feeding started 10:00 per order: Osmolite 1.5 via 16 Fr OG at 20 mL/h, advance 10 mL/h every 4 h to goal 70 mL/h (next 14:00 to 30 mL/h). Free water flush 30 mL every 4 h.
- Before starting: OG position confirmed (CXR 03:05 placement; mark at lips unchanged), suction disconnected. Initial gastric aspirate 15 mL green-clear, returned. Abdomen soft, nondistended, bowel sounds present but hypoactive x4, no stool since admission.
- HOB maintained >=30 degrees. Tolerating without retching or pulmonary changes. Residuals to be checked q4h: hold feeds and call provider for >500 mL. Feeds are not held for dressing changes (hold only for OR/extubation).

**Glucose**
- POC glucose 164 mg/dL at 10:00 (156 serum at 06:00). Stress hyperglycemia expected; recheck with 12:00 labs; insulin per protocol if persistently >180.

**Vitals (10:00)**
- HR 107 ST, BP 104/61 (MAP 75), RR 17, SpO2 100%, T 98.6 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. PIP 28/Pplat 21, FiO2 0.6, PEEP 5.

**Fluids / UOP**
- LR 225 mL/h plus feeds 20 mL/h. UOP 09-10 43 mL (0.52 mL/kg/h), in goal range. Current hour pending.

**Other**
- Oral care with chlorhexidine done at 09:00; ETT 24 cm at teeth, cuff pressure rechecked, stable. R hand Doppler present, forearm soft.
- Dietitian P. Moreno, RD consult pending; will relay tolerance and residual results.

title: Nursing Note - Midday UOP Trend, Rate Change and Family Update
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Downtrending UOP prompted call to Dr. Okafor; LR increased 225 to 270 mL/h at 14:00; family update and restraint checks.
body:
**Fluid titration**
- UOP trend: 10-11 36 mL, 11-12 32 mL, 12-13 28 mL (0.34 mL/kg/h), 13-14 28 mL (0.34 mL/kg/h). Steady decline from 43 mL/h (10:00) and below the 41 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h) target on LR 225 mL/h with MAP 76-78, urine amber.
- SBAR to Dr. Okafor by phone at 13:05: UOP below goal and downtrending; B: Parkland hour 12, 22% TBSA; A: HR 103, MAP 76, lactate 1.8 and CK 1,120 at 12:00, no myoglobinuria, PIP 27/Pplat 20, R hand Doppler intact; R: increase rate. Order: LR 225 -> 270 mL/h at 14:00 (20% increase); read back and rate changed with second-RN verification at 14:00. Feeds advanced to 30 mL/h at 14:00 per protocol. Recheck UOP hourly.

**Vitals (13:00 / 14:00)**
- HR 103 -> 102 ST, BP 105/61 (MAP 76) -> 108/63 (MAP 78), RR 17-18, SpO2 99%, T 99.0 °F. RASS -3. CPOT 1/8 at 13:00, 4/8 at 14:00 during dressing preparation; hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given at 13:45 (see dressing note). FiO2 0.5 at 14:00 per RT after 12:00 ABG (7.39/39/134, COHb 3.0%).

**Family**
- Mother Linda Delaney arrived ~11:30, tearful on first sight of patient. Jenna Whitaker and Linda at bedside. Explained ventilator, sedation, why he is asleep, hourly urine checks and fluids, wound dressings, contact precautions (gown/glove), and the plan for dressing change at 14:00. Both asked appropriate questions and verbalized understanding. Encouraged touching unburned left hand and talking to him. They stepped out for the dressing change.

**Safety**
- Soft L wrist restraint: circulation, skin, sensation checked q2h (last 14:00), skin intact, cap refill 2 s; restraint order current. ETT 24 cm at teeth. R arm elevated, hand Doppler present hourly. HOB 30.

**Plan**
- Reassess UOP at 15:00 and hourly; call burn team if <30 mL/h x2 more hours or <20 mL/h x1.

title: Nursing Note - Burn Dressing Change
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: First daily dressing change with N. Ibarra, RN at 14:00 after hydromorphone 0.5 mg; SSD to chest/R arm, bacitracin to face; tolerated.
body:
**Pre-procedure**
- Daily dressing change at 14:00 with burn nurse N. Ibarra, RN. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given at 13:45 (15 min premed). Acetaminophen 1,000 mg IV given 14:00. CPOT 1/8 before premed, 4/8 at 14:00 at start of wound manipulation. HR 102, BP 108/63 (MAP 78), SpO2 99%. Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h continued. Gown, gloves, mask, sterile technique; tube feeds continued.

**Procedure**
- Old dressings removed with saline soaks; wounds cleansed and gently debrided of loose tissue. N. Ibarra measured and photographed.
- R forearm/hand: full-thickness, leathery and waxy, escharotomy incisions clean with pink granular edges, minimal ooze. R upper arm: deep partial, moist, mottled. Anterior chest: deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches, no purulence, no odor, no erythema beyond burn margins. Face/neck: superficial to superficial partial, no drainage.
- Silver sulfadiazine 1% cream 1/16 inch applied to chest and R arm and covered with non-adherent gauze and loose wrap. Bacitracin thin layer to face after gentle cleansing.
- R hand splint reapplied in position of function (fingers MCP flexed ~70 degrees, IP extended, thumb abducted); R arm elevated on pillows above heart. Doppler radial/ulnar signals present after wrap, forearm soft, no pallor, wrap not constrictive.

**Tolerance / response**
- Procedure about 40 minutes. Transient HR rise to 108, MAP unchanged; no desaturation. CPOT 3/8 near end, CPOT 1/8 by 15:00. Propofol/fentanyl unchanged. No bleeding.

**Fluids**
- LR 270 mL/h since 14:00; UOP 14-15 37 mL (0.45 mL/kg/h), improving.

**Plan**
- Next dressing change daily 14:00. Monitor for odor, drainage, spreading erythema, eschar changes and fever. Burn nurse to follow splint adjustments with OT.

title: Nursing Note - Afternoon Update (Labs, UOP, Vent, Consults)
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: Labs trending, UOP improving, FiO2 0.5, glucose trend; PT/OT, dietitian, case management and family visits.
body:
**Vitals (17:00)**
- HR 98 ST, BP 110/65 (MAP 80), RR 17, SpO2 99%, T 99.2 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. Propofol 35 mcg/kg/min since 16:00 (comfort/vent synchrony), fentanyl 100 mcg/h.

**Labs (12:00 and 16:00)**
- K 4.9, Na 136, Cr 1.0, BUN 17, Ca 8.1 (iCa 1.05 low), Mg 1.9, Phos 3.0. CK 1,120 (02:50 480 - rising, no tea-colored urine, repeat 00:00). Lactate 1.8 -> 1.6. Hgb 13.6 (17.2 on arrival, hemodilution with resuscitation), plt 246, WBC 16.1. ABG 16:00 pH 7.40, PaCO2 38, PaO2 128, HCO3 24. COHb 3.0% at 12:00.

**Resuscitation**
- UOP 14-15 37, 15-16 38, 16-17 42 mL (0.51 mL/kg/h), back in goal range on LR 270 mL/h. Feeds 30 mL/h, advance to 40 mL/h at 18:00. Q6h bladder pressure last 11 mmHg.

**Vent**
- AC/VC VT 450, RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.5 since 14:00. PIP 27/Pplat 20. Secretions thin white-gray. ETT 24 cm at teeth. Oral care with chlorhexidine due 21:00; HOB 30.

**Glucose**
- POC 164 (10:00), serum 172 (12:00), POC 181 (16:00) - trending up with stress response and feeds; serum due 18:00. Provider aware; insulin infusion per protocol if persistently >180.

**Visits**
- PT S. Kim, PT and OT H. Larsen, OTR/L: bedside evaluation, positioning and passive ROM L side, R hand splint adjusted. P. Moreno, RD: nutrition assessment, tube feed advance plan to 70 mL/h confirmed. T. Whitfield, RN CM met Jenna and Linda about insurance and support; K. Abara, LCSW offered support resources.

**Pain / neuro / wounds**
- Dressing intact. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg given 13:45 only; CPOT 1/8 since 15:00. R hand Doppler present hourly.

**Plan**
- Hourly UOP, 18:00 labs, handoff at 19:00.

title: Nursing Note - End-of-Shift Handoff (SBAR)
author: J. Morales, RN
summary: SBAR handoff to night RN: stable on LR 270 mL/h, FiO2 0.5, UOP in range; pending 20:00 ABG and 00:00 labs.
body:
**S**
- 34 y/o M, ICU day 1, 22% TBSA flame burn + grade 2 inhalation injury, intubated and sedated. Stable shift; no pressors.

**B**
- House fire ~01:30 Mon. Parkland 7,216 mL/24 h from injury. LR 450 -> 540 (06:00) -> 225 (09:30) -> 270 mL/h (14:00). No known allergies; Full Code. Contact precautions.

**A**
- Vitals (18:00): HR 98 ST, BP 108/61 (MAP 77), RR 16, SpO2 99%, T 99.1 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8. Propofol 35 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h.
- Resp: 8.0 ETT 24 cm at teeth, AC/VC 450/16/PEEP 5, FiO2 0.5. PIP 27/Pplat 20. COHb 3.0% at 12:00. Suction thin secretions. Chlorhexidine oral care due 21:00.
- Fluids: UOP 17-18 46 mL (0.56 mL/kg/h); 14-18 range 37-46 mL/h. Cumulative LR plus EMS bolus about 6,280 mL. Feeds Osmolite 1.5 at 40 mL/h since 18:00, residual 25 mL, tolerated; next advance 22:00 to 50 mL/h.
- 18:00 labs: Na 135, K 5.0, Cr 1.0, glucose 188, Ca 7.9, Mg 1.8, Phos 2.8. Glucose >180 on two checks (181, 188); Dr. Brandt aware, recheck 22:00 and 00:00 labs, insulin infusion per protocol if still >180.
- R hand: Doppler signals present hourly, forearm soft. Dressing changed 14:00 (silver sulfadiazine chest/R arm, bacitracin face); next 14:00 Tue. Pain controlled; hydromorphone 0.5 mg at 13:45 only.
- Lines: L IJ CVC (3 lumens), L AC 18 g PIV, L radial A-line, OG, Foley. Soft L wrist restraint, skin intact. Splint on R hand.
- Family: Jenna and Linda here this afternoon, updated, will visit until ~22:30.

**R**
- 19:00 acetylcysteine neb; 20:00 ABG and albuterol; 21:00 chlorhexidine, senna-docusate, vitamin C, bacitracin to face; bowel regimen started per order; 22:00 heparin/acetaminophen, feeds to 50; 00:00 labs/CK. LR to drop to 125 mL/h at 01:30 Tue (end of 24 h Parkland). SAT planned Tue 08:00. Continue hourly UOP, neurovascular checks, q2h turns.

title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Assessment
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Night shift head-to-toe assessment; fluid status; plan for sedation interruption Tue morning.
body:
**Handoff / safety**
- Bedside handoff from J. Morales, RN at 19:00; lines, drips and restraint verified. Contact precautions, HOB 30, bed low, suction/BVM at bedside.

**Vitals (19:00)**
- HR 97 ST, BP 109/63 (MAP 78), RR 17, SpO2 98%, T 99.2 °F.

**Systems**
- Neuro: RASS -3 on propofol 35 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. Pupils 3 mm equal brisk. CPOT 1/8. CAM-ICU deferred while deeply sedated.
- Resp: 8.0 ETT 24 cm at teeth. AC/VC VT 450, RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.5; PIP 26/Pplat 19. Breath sounds coarse, diminished bases, thin white secretions. Acetylcysteine neb given 19:00.
- CV: sinus rhythm 97, MAP 78. Generalized edema. L hand warm, cap refill 2 s. R hand Doppler radial/ulnar present, forearm soft; splint on, arm elevated.
- GI: OG; Osmolite 1.5 at 40 mL/h, tolerating. Abdomen soft, nondistended, bowel sounds hypoactive. No stool yet.
- GU: Foley, amber clear urine. UOP 18-19 44 mL (0.54 mL/kg/h).
- Skin: dressings dry and intact, minimal strike-through. Face with bacitracin. Back and heels intact, low air loss mattress.
- Lines: L IJ CVC, L AC 18 g PIV, L radial A-line (zeroed at start of shift), all sites clean.
- Restraint: L wrist soft, skin intact.

**Fluid status**
- LR 270 mL/h. Cumulative LR plus EMS bolus about 6,500 mL since injury; all-source intake (LR, drips, feeds, IV meds) about 6,900 mL. Parkland goal 7,216 mL by 01:30; on track to finish above goal ("fluid creep" risk). UOP 17-18 46, 18-19 44 mL.

**Plan**
- 20:00 ABG, albuterol neb. 21:00 oral care, bowel regimen. Daily sedation interruption (SAT) Tue 08:00 with day RN and RT; propofol will be held and fentanyl continued at half dose. LR to 125 mL/h at 01:30. Check glucose with 00:00 labs.

title: Nursing Note - Pain Event / Bowel Regimen
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: CPOT 4 at 21:00 with turn and oral care; hydromorphone 0.5 mg at 21:10 with good response; bowel regimen started.
body:
**Event**
- At 21:00 during turn and oral care CPOT rose to 4/8 (grimace, tense muscle tone, brief coughing against vent). Resting CPOT 1 at 20:00. HR 97, BP 111/63 (MAP 79), RR 16, SpO2 99%: no hemodynamic change.

**Interventions**
- Paused repositioning; hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given at 21:10. Propofol 35 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h unchanged.
- Resumed turn slowly with 2 staff: supine to left side tilt, pillows between knees, heels off-loaded, burned R arm and chest not weight-bearing, R arm elevated in splint. Linens smoothed, dressings checked (intact).

**Response**
- CPOT 1/8 at 21:30, RASS -3. No oversedation; RR 16, SpO2 99%. Pain/CPOT planned before each turn.

**Bowel regimen**
- Senna-docusate 2 tablets via OG at 21:00 per bowel order (started 21:00). No stool since admission. Abdomen soft, nondistended, bowel sounds hypoactive. Stool chart started. Hold for loose stools; send C. difficile test for 3+ loose stools in 24 h.

**Other 21:00 care**
- Chlorhexidine oral rinse, vitamin C 500 mg via OG, bacitracin to face.

**Fluids / UOP**
- LR 270 mL/h. Feeds 40 mL/h, residual checked. UOP 20-21 40 mL (0.49 mL/kg/h).

**Plan**
- Premedicate before turns/ procedures as needed; reassess CPOT hourly. Continue q2h turns.

title: Nursing Note - Midnight Update
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Vent, labs, UOP in range, glucose 198; family left at 22:30.
body:
**Vitals (23:00)**
- HR 97 ST, BP 109/62 (MAP 78), RR 16, SpO2 99%, T 99.3 °F. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8 on propofol 35 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h.

**Vent**
- AC/VC VT 450, RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.5; PIP 25/Pplat 18. 20:00 ABG pH 7.40, PaCO2 39, PaO2 121, HCO3 24, SaO2 98%. Breath sounds clear to coarse, minimal thin secretions. Heparin neb 23:00, albuterol due 00:00. Oral care done 21:00.

**Labs / glucose**
- Serum glucose 188 at 18:00, POC 198 at 22:00. Dr. Brandt notified of persistent hyperglycemia; to recheck with 00:00 labs (BMP, Mg, Phos, iCa, CBC, ABG, CK) and begin insulin infusion per protocol if still >180. 18:00: K 5.0, Na 135, Ca 7.9.

**Fluids**
- LR 270 mL/h; transition to 125 mL/h planned 01:30. Feeds 50 mL/h since 22:00 (tolerating, no residual concerns). UOP: 21-22 37 mL, 22-23 38 mL (0.46 mL/kg/h). Urine amber and clear, no myoglobin concerns.

**R hand / safety**
- Doppler radial/ulnar present each hour, forearm soft, no pallor; splint on, arm elevated. L wrist restraint checked q2h (skin intact). Turned q2h; heels floated. Heparin 5,000 units SQ and acetaminophen 1,000 mg IV given 22:00.

**Family**
- Jenna Whitaker and Linda Delaney left at 22:30 after bedside visit; given the unit phone number and told they will be called for any change. Jenna asked about the ventilator and when he might wake up; explained sedation plan and that a morning wake-up trial is planned. Both appropriately tearful but coping.

**Plan**
- 00:00 labs and albuterol; hourly UOP; 01:30 LR to 125 mL/h.

title: Nursing Note - End of 24-Hour Parkland Resuscitation
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: LR changed to maintenance 125 mL/h at 01:30; totals versus Parkland goal; UOP and lab plan.
body:
**Transition**
- Per Dr. Okafor's standing order, LR decreased from 270 to 125 mL/h at 01:30 (end of 24 h from injury). Second RN verified pump rate.

**Totals vs goal**
- Parkland goal 7,216 mL (4 mL x 82 kg x 22%). LR including EMS 500 mL bolus from 01:30 Mon to 01:30 Tue: about 8,080 mL, about 12% (864 mL) over goal. First 8 h about 3,965 mL vs 3,608 goal. Overage reflects titration to UOP; monitoring for fluid creep: edema, PIP/Pplat, bladder pressure, R arm compartments.
- UOP 04:00-01:00 (ICU) 782 mL, average 37 mL/h (0.45 mL/kg/h); recent hours 38, 38, 42 mL (0.46-0.51 mL/kg/h). No hour <20 mL. Urine clear amber.

**Vitals (01:00)**
- HR 97 ST, BP 108/64 (MAP 79), RR 15, SpO2 98%, T 99.4 °F. PIP 25/Pplat 18, FiO2 0.5, PEEP 5. RASS -3, CPOT 1/8.

**Labs (00:00)**
- WBC 15.2, Hgb 12.4, plt 214; Na 134, K 4.5, Cr 1.1, BUN 21, glucose 196, Ca 7.8, iCa 1.03, Mg 1.7, Phos 2.4 (low), CK 840 (down from 1,120). ABG pH 7.41, PaCO2 40, PaO2 118, HCO3 25. Insulin infusion started 00:30 at 1 unit/h per protocol (glucose 191 at 00:30, 190 at 01:30). Phos 2.4 and Mg 1.7 reported to Dr. Brandt; recheck with 06:00 BMP.

**Neurovascular**
- R hand Doppler signals present, forearm soft, bladder pressure 12 mmHg at 23:30.

**Plan**
- Feeds 60 mL/h at 02:00. 05:00: albumin, LFTs, coags; 06:00: ABG, BMP, Mg, Phos, prealbumin, triglycerides. Albumin 5% 500 mL over 4 h at 06:00 per burn protocol. Hourly glucose on insulin infusion. SAT 08:00.

title: Nursing Note - Agitation Event / ETT Safety
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Agitation with ETT discomfort and biting, lorazepam 1 mg IV at 03:00; insulin infusion for glucose 196 started 00:30.
body:
**Event**
- ~02:45 patient became restless despite sedation (propofol 35 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h): head thrashing, bit down on ETT with ventilator high-pressure alarms, reached toward ETT with L hand. RASS rose from -3 to +1. Vitals before event 02:00: HR 96, BP 110/64 (MAP 79), SpO2 98%.

**Interventions**
- Stayed at bedside, reoriented verbally, reassured. Checked for causes: ETT 24 cm at teeth confirmed, cuff pressure 24 cmH2O, suctioned thin secretions, no kinking; ventilator asynchrony reviewed with RT. Soft L wrist restraint retained (checked: circulation, skin intact, order current); placed bite block. Pain assessed CPOT 1-2/8, no dressing/pain trigger. Hydromorphone not needed.
- Dr. Brandt (on-call intensivist) notified at 02:55 by phone (SBAR). Order: lorazepam 1 mg IV x1. Given 03:00; propofol held at 35 for now with plan to decrease to 30 at 04:00 once calm (Tuesday RASS goal -1 to -2).

**Response**
- By 03:15 RASS -3, calm, synchronous with vent, no biting. HR 93, BP 109/64 (MAP 79), RR 16, SpO2 98% at 03:00. PIP 24/Pplat 17. ETT remains 24 cm, no airway injury; lips and teeth intact, no bleeding. No unplanned extubation.

**Glucose / insulin**
- Serum glucose 196 at 00:00 (>180 persistently: 188, 198, 196); Dr. Brandt ordered insulin infusion per protocol. Regular insulin infusion started 00:30 at 1 unit/h. POC hourly: 191 (00:30), 190 (01:30), 189 (02:30). Next 03:30. Feeds 60 mL/h, LR 125 mL/h. UOP 42-43 mL/h.

**Notifications / plan**
- Charge RN B. Sutton informed. Family not present; will update Jenna at morning call. Hourly RASS/CPOT; watch for delirium (lorazepam is a delirium risk - use sparingly). Discuss SAT/sedation plan with day team at 08:00.

title: Nursing Note - Pre-Rounds Morning Update
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: Pre-rounds summary: CXR obtained, labs due, wound check, I&O night totals.
body:
**Vitals (05:00)**
- HR 93 ST, BP 110/64 (MAP 79), RR 15, SpO2 98%, T 99.5 °F. RASS -2 and CPOT 1/8 on propofol 30 mcg/kg/min (decreased 04:00) and fentanyl 100 mcg/h since lorazepam event. No further agitation.

**Resp**
- FiO2 weaned to 0.4 at 04:00; PEEP 5, VT 450, RR 16, PIP 24/Pplat 17. CXR done 05:00 at bedside: ETT/CVC positions to be confirmed by radiology read (pending). ABG due 06:00.

**Labs**
- Drawn 05:00: albumin, LFTs, coags. Due 06:00: ABG, BMP, Mg, Phos, prealbumin, triglycerides (propofol). Last POC glucose 179 at 04:30 on insulin 1 unit/h (hourly checks). 12:00 CBC/BMP/CK later.

**I&O (19:00-05:00)**
- Intake approximately 3,176 mL (LR, feeds, sedation drips, IV meds, flushes). UOP 407 mL total, average 41 mL/h (0.50 mL/kg/h). Net about +2,769 mL for night. Last hour UOP 44 mL. LR 125 mL/h until 06:00, then 75 mL/h with albumin 5% 500 mL over 4 h. Feeds 60 mL/h, at goal 70 at 06:00. Bed scale weight 89.6 kg (admit 82 kg), reflecting resuscitation edema; dosing weight remains 82 kg.

**Wounds**
- Dressings intact with moderate serosanguineous strike-through chest. Escharotomy sites clean, no odor, no spreading erythema beyond margins, face with bacitracin. R hand Doppler radial/ulnar present, forearm soft.
- Skin: sacrum and heels intact.

**Plan**
- Turn q2h, hydromorphone before AM bath/linen change if CPOT >=3. Handoff 07:00; SAT 08:00; dressing change 14:00.

title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Handoff
author: E. Haddad, RN
summary: End of night shift handoff: stable, 06:00 labs, albumin infusion, feeds at goal, SAT at 08:00.
body:
**Summary**
- ICU day 2. Stable night aside from 02:45 ETT agitation (lorazepam 1 mg IV 03:00, resolved; no recurrence). Vitals 06:00: HR 93 ST, BP 110/62 (MAP 78), RR 17, SpO2 98%, T 99.4 °F. RASS -2, CPOT 1/8 after hydromorphone 0.5 mg at 05:45 for AM turn/bath (CPOT 3 with turn).

**Drips / lines**
- Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h, insulin 1.5 units/h (since 06:00), LR 75 mL/h, albumin 5% 500 mL over 4 h started 06:00, Osmolite 1.5 at 70 mL/h (goal reached 06:00). L IJ CVC, L AC 18 g PIV, L radial A-line, OG, Foley, 8.0 ETT 24 cm at teeth. Soft L wrist restraint order active, skin intact.

**Resp**
- AC/VC 450/16/PEEP 5, FiO2 0.4; PIP 24/Pplat 17. 06:00 ABG pH 7.41, PaCO2 40, PaO2 124, HCO3 25, lactate 1.4. CXR 05:00 read pending. Chlorhexidine oral care due 09:00.

**Labs (06:00)**
- Na 134, K 3.9, Cl 108, CO2 24, BUN 23, Cr 1.1, glucose 177, Ca 7.7 (iCa 1.02), Mg 1.6 (low), Phos 2.1 (low), prealbumin 7.1, TG 168. Mg/Phos low - Dr. Brandt aware; replacement per team, recheck at 12:00. Albumin 2.6, AST 72, ALT 58, INR 1.2.

**Fluids**
- 24 h Parkland ended 01:30: LR plus EMS about 8,080 mL vs goal 7,216 mL. UOP 05-06 45 mL (0.55 mL/kg/h); night UOP 407 mL (19:00-05:00). POC glucose 182 (05:30).

**R arm / wounds**
- Hourly Doppler signals present; forearm soft. Dressings intact, no odor, no spreading erythema. Next dressing change 14:00 with burn nurse.

**Family**
- Jenna to call/visit this morning.

**Coming up**
- SAT with RT at 08:00 (propofol held, fentanyl continued at half dose); 09:00 pantoprazole/vitamins/oral care; sedation goal RASS -1 to -2; 12:00 labs.
